b2.text: Systems like AlphaEvolve rewrite whole programs, over and over, and keep whatever scores highest.

b3.text: They find remarkable solutions. But afterwards, nobody can say which idea produced the result.

b4.text: About thirty percent of the lines they add are lines they had deleted before.

b5.text: It is Darwin without Mendel: selection, but no genes.

b6.text: MendelEvolve turns every idea a language model proposes into a gene: a named switch in the solver.

b7.text: The model only invents. Classical search tunes and recombines.

b8.text: And then we do what geneticists do. We knock each gene out, and measure what is lost.

b9.text: Circle packing, starting from OpenEvolve's own program, with no hints.

b10.text: It reaches the best known value.

b11.text: Which idea did it? Knock it out.

b12.text: On fresh seeds, without this one gene, the solver loses one point six seven. One idea carries the result.

b13.text: Then, open mathematics. Problem sixty, from Tao and co-authors: points in a cube grid, with no five on a common sphere.

b14.text: MendelEvolve found larger sets than any published, at seventeen sizes.

b15.text: Each one verified by three independent exact checkers.

b16.text: Problem fifty-nine: fifty-eight points in a thirty-two by thirty-two grid, with no isosceles triangle.

b17.text: Two papers state that fifty-six is optimal.

b18.text: All thirty thousand, eight hundred and fifty-six triples check out, and DeepMind's own verifier accepts it.

b19.text: Then we turned the knockouts on our own records.

b20.text: The engine's quick screens said evolution had added nothing. They were too weak to see a fifth of a point.

b21.text: So we measured again, at record scale: six hundred paired runs per idea, both arms in the same container.

b22.text: The evolved solver is a quarter of a point better.

b23.text: And the best single idea was one the engine had thrown away. Rejected by the quick screen. Measured properly, it is worth between zero point one nine and zero point three one.

b24.text: MendelEvolve. Evolve ideas, not programs. Then measure them at the scale that matters.

b25.text: Every result, and every certificate, is public.
